content: Medical methods for preventing blood loss during a caesarean section include various techniques and interventions aimed at minimizing hemorrhage and ensuring patient safety. These methods may involve the use of uterotonic agents, such as oxytocin, to promote uterine contraction and reduce bleeding. Additionally, tranexamic acid, an antifibrinolytic agent, can be administered to stabilize blood clots and prevent excessive blood loss. Surgical techniques, such as the use of compression sutures or uterine artery ligation, may also be employed to control bleeding during the procedure. In some cases, intraoperative blood salvage or the use of cell salvage devices can help recover and reinfuse the patient’s own blood. Careful preoperative planning, including the identification of risk factors for hemorrhage, is essential to optimize outcomes and reduce the likelihood of complications.
